title: What is Sound?
concept:
Sound is vibration — rapid pressure waves moving through the air. When something vibrates, it pushes and pulls the air around it, creating these waves.

Every sound has a frequency, which determines its pitch. Frequency is measured in Hertz (Hz) — the number of vibrations per second. A low rumble has a low frequency; a high whistle has a high frequency. Humans can typically hear sounds between 20 Hz and 20,000 Hz.

Sounds also have amplitude, which determines their loudness. A larger vibration moves more air and creates a louder sound.

In this synthesizer, the Oscillator component is your sound source. It generates a continuous vibration at a frequency you control. The simplest waveform is called a sine wave — it produces a single, pure frequency with no overtones.

task.instruction: Listen to the sine wave. This is the purest form of sound — a single frequency. Notice how it sounds smooth and clear, without any grit or brightness.
